title: Map Quests: Political, Physical and Digital

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。我是罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗马·马斯。

sentences.en: The only truly accurate map of the world would be a map the size of the world.
sentences.zh: 唯一真正精准的世界地图，大概只有和世界等大的一张地图。

sentences.en: So if you want to make a map useful, something that you can hold in your hands,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想让地图变得有用，做成那种你能拿在手里的东西，

sentences.en: you have to start making choices.
sentences.zh: 你就必须开始做出取舍。

sentences.en: You have to choose what information you're interested in and what you're throwing out.
sentences.zh: 你必须选择自己对哪些信息感兴趣，又该抛弃哪些信息。

sentences.en: These choices influence how the person reading the map views the world.
sentences.zh: 这些选择会影响读图的人如何看待这个世界。

sentences.en: But a map's influence doesn't end there.
sentences.zh: 但地图的影响力并未就此结束。

sentences.en: Maps can actually shape the place they're trying to represent.
sentences.zh: 地图甚至能够塑造它们试图呈现的地方。

sentences.en: And that's when things get weird.
sentences.zh: 而事情往往就是从这里开始变得奇妙起来。

sentences.en: I love a good map.
sentences.zh: 我可太喜欢一张好地图了。

sentences.en: And today we have three short stories about how maps have changed the real world in big and small ways.
sentences.zh: 今天我们准备了三个简短的故事，讲讲地图是如何在大小不同的层面上改变现实世界的。

sentences.en: Okay, so Kurt Kolstad is in the studio with me and he also loves maps.
sentences.zh: 好的，库尔特·科尔斯特德现在跟我一起在录音室里，他也同样是个地图迷。

sentences.en: And you've written a ton of articles about maps and map projections.
sentences.zh: 你写过大量关于地图和地图投影的文章。

sentences.en: And even you did an article about the design of pins on maps.
sentences.zh: 甚至连地图上大头针的设计，你都写过文章。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，没错。

sentences.en: So the love is deep.
sentences.zh: 所以这份热爱可是相当深厚。

sentences.en: It's real.
sentences.zh: 千真万确。

sentences.en: So we're going to talk about actually one of your favorite geographical oddities,
sentences.zh: 所以我们要聊的其实是你最喜欢的地理奇观之一，

sentences.en: and that's exclaves and enclaves.
sentences.zh: 也就是飞地和内飞地。

sentences.en: And these are bits of land cut off from their home countries in various cool ways.
sentences.zh: 这些都是以各种奇妙的方式与本土分离的土地碎片。

sentences.en: Yeah, and they take a lot of forms and it gets complicated pretty faSt.
sentences.zh: 对，它们形式多样，而且很快就会变得相当复杂。

sentences.en: So I just wanted to start with something simple that, you know, listeners out there might recognize.
sentences.zh: 所以我只想从一个简单的事情开始，你知道的，听众朋友们也许能认出来。

sentences.en: When you look at a map of the United States, there's this little bump up in the middle, and it's called the Northwest Angle, and it sticks up from Minnesota into Canada.
sentences.zh: 当你看着美国地图时，中间有个小凸起，它被称为西北角，从明尼苏达州一直凸进加拿大境内。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay, I know that one.
sentences.zh: 好，这个我知道。

sentences.en: It's basically how, like, non-Minnesotans know where Minnesota is.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是，外地人用来辨认明尼苏达州在哪里标志。

sentences.en: Like, it tells it from the other states up there.
sentences.zh: 就像是用它把那上面别的州区分开来一样。

sentences.en: It just kind of breaks up this, like, clean, straight Canadian border running along the western U.S.
sentences.zh: 它有点打破了沿着美国西部延伸的那条干净、笔直的加拿大边境线。

sentences.en: And then when it hits the Great Lakes, you get this bump.
sentences.zh: 然后一到五大湖，你就会看到这个凸起。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So, like, on the left, it's all kind of a straight line, and on the right, it starts getting zigzaggy.
sentences.zh: 所以，左边基本上都是直线，到了右边就开始变得曲折了。

sentences.en: And it has a really kind of neat origin story, but I'm not going to go there today.
sentences.zh: 它的由来其实挺有意思的，但我今天就不多说了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Suffice it to say, cartographical errors were made.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，就是制图时出了错。

sentences.en: And for me, growing up in Minnesota, I actually always tended to picture this notch as a piece of land, like a solid, because, you know, it's, like, part of the shape of the map.
sentences.zh: 对在明尼苏达州长大的我来说，我其实一直倾向于把这个缺口想象成一块实体土地，就像一个整体，因为，你知道的，它毕竟是地图形状的一部分嘛。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: But it's actually not, or at least not entirely.
sentences.zh: 但实际上并非如此，或者至少不完全是。

sentences.en: So, the southern portion of the Angle is water.
sentences.zh: 西北角的南部其实是水域。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哼。

sentences.en: And above that, there is a patch of land, and that's what's known as a practical exclave.
sentences.zh: 在那片水域上方，有一小块陆地，这就是所谓的“实际飞地”。

sentences.en: A practical exclave.
sentences.zh: 实际飞地。

sentences.en: So, I know the basics of exclaves and enclaves, these are areas of land that are isolated or separated in some way from the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 我懂飞地和内飞地的基础概念，这些是与国家其他地区在某种程度上隔绝或分离的土地。

sentences.en: But what does a practical exclave mean, like, in this case?
sentences.zh: 但“实际飞地”在这个语境下到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: Basically, the land in the Angle is surrounded by Canadian land on most sides.
sentences.zh: 基本上，西北角的这片土地四周大部分都被加拿大的土地包围着。

sentences.en: But below, it has this area of American territorial water, which is, you know, basically a really big lake.
sentences.zh: 但在下方，它拥有一片属于美国的领海，说白了，其实就是一个非常大的湖。

sentences.en: So, practically speaking, someone who wants to go directly there without leaving the U.S., they could do it by boat.
sentences.zh: 所以从实际操作来看，如果有人想在不离开美国本土的情况下直接去那里，他们可以坐船前往。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But on land, they'd actually have to drive through Canada to get back into this slice of America, which isn't impossible.
sentences.zh: 但如果走陆路，他们实际上必须开车穿过加拿大才能回到这片美国的土地上，这并非不可能。

sentences.en: It's just impractical.
sentences.zh: 只是很不切实际罢了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这倒说得通。

sentences.en: This actually reminds me of Point Roberts, which we actually sent Sharif to, to do a little story a while ago, where he was, you know,
sentences.zh: 这其实让我想起了罗伯茨角，我们前不久还派沙里夫去那里做过一个小报道，他在那里，你知道的，

sentences.en: went to the post office that people go to on Point Roberts.
sentences.zh: 去了人们在罗伯茨角会去的那个邮局。

sentences.en: That's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 那挺酷的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And it's totally in that same category of exclave as Point Roberts, though in the details, they're really different.
sentences.zh: 它完全属于和罗伯茨角同一类别的飞地，尽管在细节上它们有很大不同。

sentences.en: The angle is huge.
sentences.zh: 西北角面积巨大。

sentences.en: It's much bigger.
sentences.zh: 大得多。

sentences.en: It's relatively remote, and it's really sparsely populated by comparison.
sentences.zh: 它相对偏远，相比之下人口真的非常稀少。

sentences.en: So, it only has around 100 permanent residents or so, and the crossing stations are correspondingly pretty minimaliSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，那里只有大约100名左右的常住居民，相应的过境点也非常极简。

sentences.en: So, what does it take to cross the border at the northwest angle?
sentences.zh: 那么，在西北角过境需要经历什么？

sentences.en: Well, for a long time, you had these little shack-like buildings called Outlying Area Reporting Stations, or ORS.
sentences.zh: 嗯，很长一段时间里，那里有一些被称为“边远地区报告站”（简称ORS）的小屋子一样的建筑。

sentences.en: And you had to do, like, a video call with a border agent.
sentences.zh: 你必须跟边境官员进行某种视频通话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Skype.
sentences.zh: 用Skype。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You basically Skype into the border patrol.
sentences.zh: 你基本上是通过Skype连线边境巡逻队。

sentences.en: They kind of, you know, look who wants over.
sentences.zh: 他们会，你知道的，看看是谁想过境。

sentences.en: You show them your passport, and you're on your way.
sentences.zh: 你向他们出示护照，然后就可以上路了。

sentences.en: I mean, it just wouldn't be practical to, you know, staff these things, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果要在这些地方派驻人手，那也太不切实际了吧？

sentences.en: To have a person they're unknown.
sentences.zh: 在那儿安排一个未知身份的人。

sentences.en: That's ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And then, I've been reading about this, because I haven't been up there in a while.
sentences.zh: 然后，我最近一直在看这方面的报道，因为我有一阵子没去那边了。

sentences.en: And apparently, over the last few years, they've been working on streamlining things with a mobile app called Roam, spelled R-O-A-M.
sentences.zh: 显然，在过去几年里，他们一直在通过一个名为Roam（拼写为R-O-A-M）的手机应用来简化流程。

sentences.en: So, like, a way that you can kind of check in without really going through all these hoops.
sentences.zh: 所以，这相当于找到了一种不用经历那么多繁文缛节就能进行登记的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's so cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: So, you have Point Roberts, you have Northwest Angle.
sentences.zh: 所以，你有罗伯茨角，也有西北角。

sentences.en: You know, these are fairly regional examples.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些都是相当区域化的例子。

sentences.en: Like, people that live there interact with them, but most people don't interact with them.
sentences.zh: 就像，住在那里的人会与它们产生交集，但大多数人并不会。

sentences.en: Are there ones that have, like, bigger impacts on the world in general?
sentences.zh: 有没有那种对整个世界产生更大影响的例子？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: I mean, there's ones that people never really think about.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些是人们从不会真正想到的。

sentences.en: And a really good example is the whole state of Alaska.
sentences.zh: 一个非常好的例子就是整个阿拉斯加州。

sentences.en: Okay, of course.
sentences.zh: 好吧，当然。

sentences.en: So, Alaska is considered to be what's called a semi-exclave.
sentences.zh: 所以，阿拉斯加被认为是所谓的“半飞地”。

sentences.en: And it's actually the largest of its kind in the world.
sentences.zh: 它实际上也是世界上同类中最大的一块。

sentences.en: And it's got this semi-modifier, because even though it doesn't border the lower 48, it does have, like, this really long stretch of international coastline.
sentences.zh: 之所以带有“半”这个修饰词，是因为尽管它与美国本土48州不接壤，但它确实拥有非常长的一段国际海岸线。

sentences.en: So, it really has direct access to international waters.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实可以直接通往国际水域。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay, so those are exclaves.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这些是飞地。

sentences.en: I think those are pretty easy to understand.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这些挺容易理解的。

sentences.en: So, describe what enclaves are, because those can be pretty strange.
sentences.zh: 那么请描述一下什么是内飞地，因为那些可能相当奇特。

sentences.en: They really can.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I should note here that there are some nuances to all this and a lot of complexity.
sentences.zh: 我在这里需要指出，所有这些概念都有一些细微差别，而且非常复杂。

sentences.en: Like, some enclaves are also exclaves.
sentences.zh: 比如，有些内飞地同时也是飞地。

sentences.en: But, like, in the simplest and most general terms, enclaves are countries or parts of countries that are entirely contained within another country's territory.
sentences.zh: 但是，用最简单、最通俗的术语来说，内飞地是指完全包含在另一个国家领土之内的国家或国家的一部分。

sentences.en: So, they're totally surrounded.
sentences.zh: 所以它们是被完全包围的。

sentences.en: So, Northwest Angle and Point Roberts in Alaska, they don't count, because they aren't cut off completely from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，西北角、罗伯茨角和阿拉斯加都不算，因为它们并没有与美国完全切断。

sentences.en: So, you can still get to these places by boat, for example.
sentences.zh: 所以你仍然可以乘船等方式到达这些地方。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: Whereas, enclaves are fully enclosed.
sentences.zh: 而内飞地则是完全封闭的。

sentences.en: So, San Marino in Europe is a classic example.
sentences.zh: 欧洲的圣马力诺就是一个经典的例子。

sentences.en: It's this relatively small country, and it's completely enclaved on all sides by Italy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相对较小的国家，四周完全被意大利合围。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe it's because the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我是说，也许是因为美国

sentences.en: is so isolated and on its own and surrounded by water that that feels weird to me to be enclosed in another country.
sentences.zh: 太孤立、太独立且四面环水，所以被另一个国家包围这种事对我来说感觉很诡异。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe if you're, like, the Czech Republic, you're surrounded by other countries.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许如果你像捷克共和国那样，你会被其他国家包围。

sentences.en: Yeah, or, like, Luxembourg or something.
sentences.zh: 对，或者像卢森堡之类的。

sentences.en: It's like, you know, it might not be one country, but you're still pretty small.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，你知道的，虽然可能不止一个国家，但你的面积依然很小。

sentences.en: But there's still something kind of special about being a country completely inside one other country.
sentences.zh: 但作为一个完全位于另一个单一国家内部的国家，还是有一种相当特别的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, you're kind of dependent on them in certain curious ways.
sentences.zh: 对，对，你在某种奇特的方式上要依附于他们。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，完全正确。

sentences.en: And that's sort of just the first level of this, too.
sentences.zh: 而这仅仅是这一概念的第一层。

sentences.en: These things get even more complex and even more small in a lot of cases.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，这些情况变得更加复杂，甚至更加微小。

sentences.en: For example, with counter enclaves, which are an enclave inside of another enclave, or more specifically, like,
sentences.zh: 例如，反向内飞地，也就是内飞地内部的内飞地，或者更具体地说，比如，

sentences.en: a piece of the Netherlands inside a piece of Belgium that is itself in the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 一块属于荷兰的土地夹在了一块属于比利时的土地里，而这块比利时土地本身又位于荷兰境内。

sentences.en: So they're, like, second order enclaves, or, like, enclaves in enclaves.
sentences.zh: 所以它们就像是第二层内飞地，或者说，内飞地套内飞地。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Enclaves all the way down.
sentences.zh: 内飞地套内飞地，无穷无尽。

sentences.en: All the way down.
sentences.zh: 没完没了。

sentences.en: And as crazy as those are, it doesn't stop there.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些已经够疯狂了，但这还没完。

sentences.en: Consider counter-counter enclaves.
sentences.zh: 想想反向反向内飞地。

sentences.en: Like, a piece of India inside a piece of Bangladesh inside a piece of India inside a Bangladesh.
sentences.zh: 比如，一块印度的土地被包围在一块孟加拉国的土地里，而这块孟加拉国的土地又被包围在一块印度的土地里，这块印度土地又在孟加拉国内。

sentences.en: And, in fact, that triple enclave example is the only known third order enclave in world history.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那个三重内飞地的例子是世界历史上唯一已知的第三层内飞地。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, that makes sense that it would be the only one because it's so absurd.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这倒也合理，它会是唯一的一个，因为这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: It's pretty, yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实，对。

sentences.en: I mean, it's pretty hard to picture.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这很难想象。

sentences.en: So how does that even work in the real world?
sentences.zh: 那么这在现实世界中到底是怎么运作的呢？

sentences.en: So basically, for a long time, there were villages within villages.
sentences.zh: 基本上，在很长一段时间里，那是村中之村。

sentences.en: And at the middle of it all was this two-acre parcel that was owned by a Bangladeshi farmer who lived in the surrounding enclave.
sentences.zh: 而这一切的核心是一块两英亩的土地，由一名住在周围内飞地里的孟加拉国农民拥有。

sentences.en: And he would just wake up in the morning and cross into India to farm his tiny patch of land in the middle of this zone.
sentences.zh: 他每天早上醒来，穿境进入印度，去耕种这片位于该区域中心的土地。

sentences.en: And then he would cross back into Bangladesh each night.
sentences.zh: 然后每天晚上再穿境回到孟加拉国。

sentences.en: In 2015, India and Bangladesh finally agreed to this really big cross-border land swap to essentially tidy up all these enclaves within enclaves.
sentences.zh: 2015年，印度和孟加拉国终于同意进行这场非常大的跨国土地置换，本质上是为了清理所有这些错综复杂的内飞地。

sentences.en: And essentially, they ended up handing over dozens of enclaves to each other, totaling thousands of acres.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，他们最终向彼此移交了数十块内飞地，总面积达数千英亩。

sentences.en: Did that mean that there were, like, Indians now living in Bangladesh and vice versa?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着，现在有印度人住在孟加拉国，反之亦然？

sentences.en: I mean, yes, in some cases.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的，在某些情况下确实如此。

sentences.en: And I actually thought they handled it pretty well and pragmatically.
sentences.zh: 我其实觉得他们处理得很好，也很务实。

sentences.en: They basically offered residents of these former enclaves a choice.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上给这些前内飞地的居民提供了一个选择。

sentences.en: They could either stay where they were and basically be in a different country than they had been before.
sentences.zh: 他们既可以留在原地，实际上就身处于一个与以往不同的国家。

sentences.en: Or they could move, quote-unquote, back across the border to their official country of citizenship.
sentences.zh: 也可以选择“搬迁”，也就是搬回他们拥有公民身份的官方祖国。

sentences.en: And it all kind of reminds me, like, this isn't quite technically an enclave or an exclave thing.
sentences.zh: 这一切让我想起，这虽然在严格意义上不算是一处内飞地或飞地的事情。

sentences.en: But once you start thinking in these terms, there are some other interesting geographical mind-benders out there.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你开始用这种方式思考，外面还有其他一些有趣的地理烧脑问题。

sentences.en: So I've got one more for you.
sentences.zh: 所以我还有一个要跟你分享。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好啊。

sentences.en: And as far as I know, this place has no official name.
sentences.zh: 而且据我所知，这个地方没有官方名称。

sentences.en: So I've just been calling it Inception Island.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直叫它“盗梦空间岛”。

sentences.en: Okay.
